title: RateLimit
description: A request-throttling policy attached to an API's servers, paths or operations that caps how many requests a consumer, identified by a counting key, may make within a fixed time window. It also states what enforcement happens when that cap is exceeded. Use Header instead when you are modelling the response headers that report quota state to clients (e.g. X-RateLimit-Remaining, RateLimit-Reset, Retry-After), not the limit policy itself. Use Response instead when you are modelling the documented HTTP outcome returned when a limit trips (typically 429 Too Many Requests or 503), including its description and body. Use SecurityScheme instead when the element defines how a caller is authenticated (an API key, bearer token or OAuth2), even if that identity is later used as the rate-limit key.

requests.description: Maximum number of requests permitted within the specified time window.

window.description: Duration of the rate limit window (e.g., '1m', '1h', '24h'). Requests are counted and reset per window.

scope.description: Scope at which the rate limit is applied.

action.description: Action taken when the rate limit is exceeded, per NIST SC-5 (Denial-of-Service Protection).

keyBy.description: Attribute used to identify and group requests for rate limit counting (e.g., 'user.id', 'request.ip', 'api-key').

x-dr-standard: No OpenAPI 3.0 object; typically expressed as a vendor extension (e.g. x-ratelimit) or in gateway config; enforcement action aligns with NIST SP 800-53 SC-5 Denial-of-Service Protection.
x-dr-evidence: Rate-limiting middleware mounted on an HTTP router with numeric limits, e.g. express-rate-limit `rateLimit({ windowMs: 60000, max: 100, keyGenerator })` or ASP.NET `AddRateLimiter`/`[EnableRateLimiting]`.

Framework throttle declarations on handlers or controllers, e.g. NestJS `@Throttle({ default: { limit: 10, ttl: 60000 } })`, Django REST Framework `throttle_classes` with `DEFAULT_THROTTLE_RATES = {'user': '1000/day'}`, or Spring/Bucket4j bucket definitions.

API gateway or proxy configuration defining request quotas per route or consumer, e.g. a Kong `rate-limiting` plugin, an AWS API Gateway usage plan throttle, an nginx `limit_req_zone`, or an `x-ratelimit` extension in the OpenAPI file.

x-dr-distinguish.api.header: you are modelling the response headers that report quota state to clients (e.g. X-RateLimit-Remaining, RateLimit-Reset, Retry-After), not the limit policy itself.
x-dr-distinguish.api.response: you are modelling the documented HTTP outcome returned when a limit trips (typically 429 Too Many Requests or 503), including its description and body.
x-dr-distinguish.api.securityscheme: the element defines how a caller is authenticated (an API key, bearer token or OAuth2), even if that identity is later used as the rate-limit key.
